title: Affine evaluation of the higher-image limit cocone
statement: Let Λ be any commutative ring, k:W→S and G a Λ-module sheaf on W_et [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let I be a small cofiltered category and D:I→Over W have affine transition morphisms and qcqs structure maps to S. Let c be a cone whose underlying cone of schemes is limiting, with qcqs structure map to S. Fix q∈ℤ. Let K:I^op→Sh(S_et,Λ) be presented by isomorphisms eK_i:K(i)≅R^qg_i,*G_i, where g_i:D(i)→S and G_i=D(i)^*G, and require its arrows to be eK_i≫t(D(f))≫eK_j^-1, for the canonical transitions of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions]. Let B be a cocone presented by eB:B.pt≅R^qg_*G_c and legs eK_i≫t(c_i)≫eB^-1. For every affine etale object V→S, evaluation of B on V is a colimit cocone in Λ-modules. Inverse images and higher direct images are as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: An injective module resolution computes underlying abelian section cohomology on every etale object because its terms are abelian-section-acyclic (03FD). Forgetting scalars is exact and conservative; all the canonical maps are linear. This transports the abelian cohomology and higher-image descriptions to module sheaves without assuming that Λ is flat over ℤ.

If needed replace I^op by a small directed final category. The opposite presentation is initial, so it computes the same scheme limit. For an affine etale object U→S base change gives qcqs schemes U×_S D(i) and U×_S c.pt, affine transitions, and a limiting cone. The pulled-back sheaves on the limit canonically identify with the pullback of G and have identity transition maps under those identifications. Since I^op is nonempty and connected, this is their colimit.

Regard the sheaves as complexes in degree zero, with common lower bound zero. Continuity for systems of complexes gives the canonical cohomology colimit comparison on each affine etale U. Its maps are derived adjunction units and commute with restriction. For q<0 use the vanishing of cohomology of a sheaf resolution in negative degrees.

By the higher-image presheaf description the objects are sheafifications of the restricted cohomology presheaves. The comparisons in the preceding step are isomorphisms on the affine basis. Sheafification commutes with colimits, so these local comparisons yield the higher-image sheaf colimit comparison. The specified hK and hB identify its arrows and legs with those of B.

Every covering of affine V admits a finite affine refinement with quasi-compact overlaps. Filtered colimits of modules commute with the finite products and equalizers in the sheaf condition. Equivalently apply Sites 0738(4) to sections and use exact forgetting of module operations. Hence evaluation on V preserves filtered colimits. Evaluate the comparison from the preceding step to obtain precisely the universal property stated here.
